rounds.question: Name a reason the United States entered World War II

answers.explanation: This is a reason the US entered WWII — the December 7, 1941 attack on the US naval base killed 2,400 Americans and ended isolationism.

answers.text: Germany declared war on the US
answers.explanation: This is a reason the US entered WWII — Hitler declared war four days after Pearl Harbor, bringing the US into the European theater.
This is a reason the US entered WWII — FDR framed the war as a global struggle between fascism and democratic freedom.

answers.text: US already supplying Allies via Lend-Lease
answers.explanation: This is a reason the US entered WWII — the US was already deeply invested in Allied victory before Pearl Harbor formalized the commitment.

answers.text: End of isolationism after Pearl Harbor
answers.explanation: This is a reason the US entered WWII — the attack shattered domestic opposition to involvement that had been strong through 1941.

rounds.question: Name a sacrifice Americans made on the home front during WWII

answers.explanation: This is a home front sacrifice — Americans used ration books for meat, sugar, butter, and gasoline to ensure supplies reached the military.
This is a home front sacrifice — 'Rosie the Riveter' became an icon as women took industrial jobs vacated by men who joined the military.
This is a home front sacrifice — Americans bought billions in bonds, deferring consumption to finance the war.
This is a home front sacrifice — auto plants switched to tanks and jeeps; appliance makers produced weapons; the entire economy mobilized.
This is a home front sacrifice — families grew their own vegetables to free up commercial food for military use.

rounds.question: Name a turning point or major event of World War II

answers.explanation: This is a WWII turning point — the June 6, 1944 Allied landing in France opened the Western Front and began the liberation of Europe.

answers.text: Battle of Midway in the Pacific
answers.explanation: This is a WWII turning point — the June 1942 naval battle destroyed Japan's carrier fleet and shifted momentum in the Pacific.
This is a WWII turning point — the bombs on Hiroshima and Nagasaki in August 1945 led directly to Japan's surrender.
This is a WWII turning point — the German defeat at Stalingrad in 1943 marked the beginning of the Nazi retreat on the Eastern Front.
This is a WWII event — Operation Torch in 1942 gave the Allies experience and set the stage for the invasion of Italy.

rounds.question: Name a civil liberties violation that occurred during WWII

answers.explanation: This is a WWII civil liberties violation — Executive Order 9066 forcibly relocated 120,000 Japanese Americans to prison camps.

answers.text: Korematsu v. United States upheld it
answers.explanation: This is a WWII civil liberties violation — the Supreme Court upheld internment; the decision was formally repudiated in 2018.
This is a WWII civil liberties violation — FDR's order authorized the military to designate 'exclusion zones' and remove Japanese Americans.

answers.text: Suspension of due process for citizens
answers.explanation: This is a WWII civil liberties violation — Japanese Americans were imprisoned without trial, charge, or individual review.
This is a WWII civil liberties issue — Black soldiers served in segregated units; the Double V campaign demanded victory over fascism and racism.

rounds.question: Name an outcome or consequence of World War II

answers.explanation: This is a WWII outcome — the UN replaced the failed League of Nations as a forum for international cooperation.

answers.text: Start of the Cold War with USSR
answers.explanation: This is a WWII outcome — wartime alliance with the Soviets dissolved quickly as competing visions for postwar Europe emerged.
This is a WWII outcome — the war destroyed rival economies while the US emerged stronger, becoming the dominant world power.
This is a WWII outcome — the trials established the precedent of prosecuting war crimes and crimes against humanity.
This is a WWII outcome — the war weakened European colonial powers and emboldened independence movements in Asia and Africa.

rounds.question: Name a debate surrounding the decision to drop the atomic bomb

answers.text: Saved lives by avoiding an invasion
answers.explanation: This is an argument in the atomic bomb debate — proponents said an invasion of Japan would have killed hundreds of thousands on both sides.

answers.text: Killed hundreds of thousands of civilians
answers.explanation: This is an argument in the atomic bomb debate — critics argue targeting civilian populations constituted a war crime.

answers.text: Japan was already close to surrender
answers.explanation: This is an argument in the atomic bomb debate — some historians argue Japan was seeking terms before the bombs fell.

answers.text: Sent a message to the Soviet Union
answers.explanation: This is an argument in the atomic bomb debate — some historians believe the bombs were partly intended to intimidate the USSR.
This is an argument in the atomic bomb debate — the bombs launched a decades-long superpower competition in nuclear weapons.
